absent: Locking, concurrency, and sleep-context rules for the helpers are not shown.
Full layouts of struct pci_dev, struct pci_bus, struct device, struct device_node, and struct eeh_dev beyond the referenced members are not shown.
How MSI domains are created or looked up outside the null fallback, and how PR3 or removability are decided on other configurations, are not shown.
Behaviour of pci_upstream_bridge, pci_name, dev logging, and WARN helpers beyond how they are invoked here is not shown.
Meaning and allocation of PCI_DEV_FLAGS_ASSIGNED and other flag bits besides assignment are not shown.

findings.text: In this configuration the host bridge OF MSI lookup yields no domain and the OF MSI mapping probe reports absence, indicating MSI mapping through device tree is unavailable.
Device and bus helpers expose the associated firmware node by returning the embedded generic device node pointer, tolerating a null input by returning null instead of dereferencing.
In this configuration the host bridge ACPI MSI lookup yields no domain and the PR3 presence probe reports absence, indicating those platform features are unavailable.
The architecture removable-device query reports that no PCI device is removable in this configuration.
A PCI device exposes its platform error-handling descriptor through the architecture data area of its embedded generic device.
Device assignment state is held in a flag word on the PCI device: one operation sets the assigned bit, one clears it, and a predicate reports whether the bit is set.
Alternate routing interpretation is reported enabled for a bus only when the bus has an upstream device and that device records ARI as enabled.
Thunderbolt attachment is true when the device itself is flagged or any upstream bridge obtained by repeatedly following the upstream bridge link is flagged; otherwise it is false.

PCI logging helpers forward severity, once-only, and rate-limited diagnostics to the corresponding generic device logging facility using the embedded generic device, while warning helpers also include the driver name and PCI device name.

Observed PCI device state includes an embedded generic device carrying a firmware node and architecture error descriptor, a flag word holding assignment state, a Thunderbolt marker, and an ARI enabled marker.
Observed PCI bus state includes an embedded generic device carrying a firmware node and an optional pointer to the upstream bridge device.
Firmware node helpers accept null and return null; the error descriptor, assigned flag, ARI, Thunderbolt, and removable helpers require a valid device or bus pointer and do not show null handling.
Setting then testing assignment reports assigned, clearing then testing reports unassigned, and testing checks only the assigned bit.
Callers must ensure non-null arguments for the error descriptor, assigned flag, ARI, and Thunderbolt helpers because the fragments show direct member access without validation.
Header guard identifier _LINUX_PCI_IDS_H is defined to protect the PCI identifiers header from multiple inclusion.
